panels.title: Speech: should pupils choose their leaders?
points: Hook: Who chose the last leader you followed?
Context: Next term, our class leaders will be appointed.
Position: I will argue that pupils should elect their own leaders, because leadership is earned by trust.
Preview: fairness, responsibility and growth
Answer: A purposeful introduction

panels.title: Point 1: fairness
points: Point: Firstly, electing leaders is fairer.
Evidence: When leaders are appointed, pupils often say they had no voice.
Explain: A vote gives every pupil an equal say.
Develop: Over time, this builds trust, because people respect leaders they chose.
Answer: A developed persuasive paragraph

panels.title: Upgrade: Pupils should have a say in who leads them.
points: Inclusive pronoun: We should have a say...
Anaphora: We deserve a voice. We deserve a choice.
Rhetorical question: Why should leadership be decided for us?
Check: does each method serve the point?
Answer: We deserve a voice. We deserve a choice. Why should leadership be decided for us, and not by us?

panels.title: Signpost the speech
points: After the position: I have three reasons.
Point 1: Firstly, consider fairness.
Point 2: Moreover, think about responsibility.
Point 3: Crucially, elections help us grow.
Answer: A clearly signposted speech
